title: Slovenian meat plant says hackers changed a freezer setting to 100°C and locked out a technician
date_note: The page gives only its publication day, 27 November, and no date for the incident.
geo_basis: victim city stated: the plant is in Tolmin, Slovenia
summary: Cyber Security News, citing an interview with the cooperative's director Nikola Šavle and the Slovenian Press Agency, reports hackers changed a freezer chamber's setting to 100°C at the Salamerija Alpija plant in Tolmin, and a technician was locked out of the cooling control system. Staff caught the change and no meat spoiled, the director said. Staff also found a store refrigerator set to 20°C instead of its usual 2–3°C. The article names no culprit.
plain: At a Slovenian meat plant someone changed a freezer's target temperature to 100°C and blocked a technician's login. Staff noticed in time, according to the cooperative's director.
exec: A food producer's cooling controls were altered remotely; staff caught it and, per the director, no meat spoiled.
action: General advice: the article suggests inventorying OT assets, removing direct internet access to control equipment, and alerting on unexpected changes to target temperature settings.

evidence.quote: Hackers changed a freezer chamber’s temperature setting to 100°C at Salamerija Alpija
a refrigerator at one of their stores had been set to 20°C instead of its usual 2–3°C.

validation.note: Only Cyber Security News was read; it cites a 24ur interview and the Slovenian Press Agency, neither read directly.

review.note: Compared title, 100C/20C/2-3C, director statement, no culprit, advice against Cyber Security News
